historical_claims.claim: Changing magnetic flux inducing electromotive force associated with Michael Faraday; direction of induced effects associated with Heinrich Lenz
historical_claims.location: §13.1; original historical primary sources not independently researched

evidence_claims.limitations: Historical attributions are specific to induction; modern transformers were developed by many contributors.

evidence_claims.claim: Ideal transformer secondary-to-primary voltage ratio equals turns ratio
evidence_claims.limitations: Assumes perfect coupling, no losses, intended AC waveform/frequency.

evidence_claims.claim: Ideal output and input apparent power, inverse current ratio
evidence_claims.limitations: Not a nameplate/current-rating substitute; model omits magnetizing current.

evidence_claims.claim: Higher voltage can reduce I-squared-R line losses at fixed transferred power
evidence_claims.limitations: Only under fixed power, conductor resistance and assumptions; insulation/clearances change.

evidence_claims.claim: Real transformer has core and copper losses, finite nameplate ratings
evidence_claims.limitations: Actual thermal and input/output ratings require manufacturer data and qualified review.

evidence_claims.claim: Inrush, saturation and incompatible frequency/waveform can defeat ideal calculations
evidence_claims.limitations: Specific inrush and saturation behavior requires full component data; independent corroboration outstanding.

evidence_claims.claim: Two-winding versus autotransformer is not the same isolation architecture
evidence_claims.limitations: Protective isolation and insulation testing require product standard and exact model.

evidence_claims.claim: Conventional transformer needs varying flux; DC inverter uses active conversion
evidence_claims.limitations: Steady DC incompatible with ordinary mains-frequency transformer model; no inverter design or connection approval.

evidence_claims.claim: Backfeed and alternate sources need verified isolation and integration
evidence_claims.limitations: Home source transfer requires adopted code and equipment-specific professional review.

evidence_claims.claim: A conductor called neutral is not automatically touch-safe

supports.location: OSHA July 2003 interpretation of open neutral

evidence_claims.limitations: Exact system arrangement varies; no individual safe-contact inference.

evidence_claims.claim: Worked turns, current and loop-loss calculations follow ideal definitions
evidence_claims.limitations: Independently recalculated; not a physical device specification.

evidence_review.scope: claim-level checks of public explanations, regulatory provisions, published standards scope and selected engineering material; original calculations cross-checked
evidence_review.claim_level_corroboration: Partial; individual claim entries identify evidence and gaps

description: Explains magnetic fields and induction through a transformer’s coupled windings, connecting voltage transformation to electrical transmission and energy transfer.
tags: Two windings and one changing flux
